the future risk of a myocardial infarct is commonly assessed using classical risk predictors, but that low-attenuating plaque burden on coronary computed tomography angiography (CtA) might be better predictor.
the future risk of MI is commonly assessed using CV risk scores, coronary calcification and coronary artery stenotic severity.

the presence of low attenuation plaque is a strong predictor of myocardial events in patients with stable coronary artery disease.

noncalcified low attenuation plaque burden on coronary CTA predicts myocardial infarctions.

the burden of low-attenuating plaque, a novel biomarker of coronary atherosclerosis, may be a more powerful predictor of myocardial injury than traditional cardiovascular risk scores or coronary calcium score.
